 DAL

 Player Stats

 Zaccharie Risacher led the Mavericks with 22 points (9-of-14 FGs), six rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and four three-pointers in a 133-94 loss to the Timberwolves on Thursday.
 Risacher was the leading scorer for Dallas in this game, though most of his work came after the result had been decided. Risacher had a strong start to the season, specifically on the defensive end. However, he has cooled off a bit in recent weeks, though this was a nice outing for him. However, in the month of November, he has only scored in double figures in the games that were decided by at least 35 points, making him a difficult player to trust in fantasy basketball.
 -  Noah Rubin

 The Dallas Mavericks will start Kyrie Irving, Caleb Martin, Cooper Flagg, PJ Washington, and Daniel Gafford against the Jazz. 
 The Mavericks made one change to their starting lineup from last game which is that Caleb Martin is replacing Zaccharie Risacher in the starting lineup. Risacher should still have an important role off the bench in this game, so there shouldn’t be much that changes in their value. Risacher played 18 minutes last game while Caleb Martin played 20 minutes.

 Cooper Flagg (shoulder) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Heat. 
 Flagg being listed as questionable on the Mavericks’ initial injury report is good news for fantasy managers. After he sustained a shoulder injury during Friday’s win over the Pacers, expectations were that the reigning Rookie of the Year would miss a few days. Now, Flagg could miss just one game after sitting out Saturday’s loss to the Spurs. If he returns, Zaccharie Risacher will head to the bench.

 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher recorded 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal, two blocks and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs. 
 After Cooper Flagg sustained a left shoulder injury in Friday’s win over the Pacers, Risacher started for the Mavericks for the first time on Saturday. He had a highlight-worthy block on Victor Wembanyama at the rim in the first half, but his overall production wasn’t enough to put Risacher on the streaming radar. Naji Marshall and PJ Washington (12 points, four rebounds and two assists) are better fantasy options until Flagg returns.

 Bones Hyland led the Timberwolves with 24 points (7-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, eight assists, two steals and five three-pointers in a 133-94 win over the Mavericks on Thursday.
 Hyland had his best game of the season in what ended up being a blowout win for Minnesota. He set season highs for both points and three-pointers while matching his season high for assists. Hyland has been a solid reserve for the Wolves this season, though the production hasn’t come consistently. Despite a fantastic performance, he isn’t worth adding in most formats due to a limited role.

 LaMelo Ball lit up the Mavericks with 22 points (8-of-14 FGs), three rebounds, nine assists, two steals and six three-pointers on Thursday.
 It wasn’t a monster game for LaMelo, but it didn’t need to be. He made the most of his 25 minutes on the court in the blowout win. This was his fifth straight game with at least 20 points, and he set a new season high for assists. LaMelo took some time to get going, but he is starting to get into a groove with Anthony Edwards sidelined. Minnesota has now won five straight games and will look to extend their streak with the Bulls coming to town on Saturday.

 P.J. Washington finished with 10 points (4-of-7 FGs), three rebounds and one three-pointer against the Timberwolves on Thursday.
 Washington got off to a hot start to this game, scoring 10 points in the first quarter. Unfortunately, foul trouble limited him to just 16 minutes, and he didn’t score over the final three quarters. That pretty much sums this game up for Dallas, as they were outscored by 31 points after the first quarter. They were completely dominated in this game, though Washington was able to start off well, so that is something, I suppose. They’ll look to bounce back in Cleveland on Saturday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Trae Young

 Trae Young led the Wizards with 37 points (8-of-23 FGs, 17-of-17 FTs), two rebounds, 14 assists and four three-pointers in a 144-140 loss to the Pistons in double overtime on Thursday.
 A big fourth quarter led to Trae setting a new season high for scoring. In fact, this was his first 30-point, 10-assist game as a Wizard and the 92nd of his career, which ranks fifth in NBA history. Unfortunately, after scoring his 33rd point at the buzzer with an incredible three-pointer to force overtime, he shot 0-of-7 from the floor in overtime, with the four extra points coming at the free throw line. Still, it was an excellent night for him and was certainly his best performance as a Wizard. It is also worth noting that AJ Dybantsa, despite a rough night, hit a tough mid-range shot to force the second overtime, which was a fun moment for the rookie.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Anthony Davis recorded a double-double on Thursday with 30 points (13-of-21 FGs), 15 rebounds, four assists and one steal against the Pistons.
 Though he ended up fouling out early in the second overtime, AD still had more than enough time to make his impact felt in this game. This was his fourth straight game with at least 20 points and 10 rebounds, though he was able to set a new season high for boards in this one. Though AD will always have his question marks, he’s one of the most dominant players in fantasy basketball when he’s on the court. He’ll look to stay hot against the Rockets to wrap up the week on Sunday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Alex Sarr lit up the Pistons on Thursday with 30 points (12-of-14 FGs), nine rebounds, two assists, two steals, one block and four three-pointers.
 It has been a rough start to the season for Sarr, especially on the offensive end. However, he was excellent in this one. He set a new season high for scoring and started the game shooting 10-of-10 from the floor. He didn’t miss a shot until overtime. This was the fourth 30-point game of his career, and it was by far his best outing of the season. Hopefully this is the type of performance he’ll be able to build on after a slow start to the year.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Paul Reed provided a boost off the bench with 13 points (5-of-9 FGs), 11 rebounds and three assists against the Wizards on Thursday.
 Reed may have been bumped to the bench two games ago, but that doesn’t mean his value is gone. He proved that in this game, and he was part of the closing lineup instead of John Collins. Keep an eye on the starting lineup for their next game in Miami on Saturday. Reed could return to the starting unit, but even if he doesn’t, he should play enough to be worth rostering.
 -  Noah Rubin 
 Recap

 Ausar Thompson 
 DET 
 Guard-Forward 
 #9 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Ausar Thompson stuffed the stat sheet on Thursday with 17 points (8-of-15 FGs), 11 rebounds, 11 assists, three steals and three blocks against the Wizards.
 Thompson did a little bit of everything for Detroit in this game, which included the first triple-double of his career and a new career high for assists to go with a massive impact on the defensive end. Thompson’s rebounding and assist numbers have been way up to start the season, which has helped make up for a drop in defensive stats and field goal percentage, though he was excellent in all of those categories in this one. He is one of the best defensive players in the league, and he was able to get it done on offensive as well on Thursday.
 -  Noah Rubin 
 Recap 
 More Ausar Thompson News
 Cade Cunningham 
 DET 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Cade Cunningham led the Pistons with 52 points (16-of-25 FGs, 17-of-18 FTs), five rebounds, 11 assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in a 144-140 double overtime win over the Wizards on Thursday.
 Cunningham set a new career high for scoring in this game, with 30 of those 52 coming in the fourth quarter and overtime. However, the most impressive part of his performance was that he didn’t turn the ball over once, which led to him becoming the first player with at least 50 points and 10 assists in a game without turning it over. This was one of the best games anyone has had this season, and it came after he scored a total of 31 points over Detroit’s last two games. It was good to see him not only get back on track, but to truly dominate. He’ll look to carry some of this production with him to Miami on Saturday to wrap up the week.
 -  Noah Rubin
